text: I. Professional Core PositioningThis major focuses on "the industrialization of chemical processes", covering the entire process from raw materials to products: including the optimization of chemical reactions, the transmission and separation of materials, the design and scaling-up of equipment, and the control and optimization of production processes. The aim is to enhance production efficiency, reduce energy consumption, and minimize pollution through engineering techniques, achieving efficient, green, and safe operation of chemical production. The core logic is the transformation chain of "laboratory small-scale trial → pilot-scale amplification → industrial production".II. Training ObjectivesTo cultivate high-quality engineering talents with solid knowledge of chemical engineering and technology, proficient in core capabilities such as process design, process optimization, equipment selection, and system integration, and capable of engaging in scientific research, technology development, engineering design, and production management in fields such as chemical engineering, energy, materials, medicine, and environmental protection. Specific requirements include: Master the basic principles of chemical reaction engineering, chemical thermodynamics, and transfer processes;Have the ability to design chemical processes (such as reactor selection, separation process design) and perform equipment calculations (such as determining parameters of heat exchangers, distillation towers);Be familiar with chemical process simulation software (such as Aspen Plus, COMSOL) and automation control technologies;Understand the cutting-edge fields and industry standards in chemical safety, green chemistry, and process intensification.
